findings.issue_text: Unguarded nil dereferences in TopicsController#unsubscribe cause 500s on the primary email-link flow: current_user is nil for anonymous requests (opening an email link while logged out) so current_user.id raises NoMethodError instead of redirecting to login; TopicUser.find_by returns nil when the logged-in account has no topic_users row for the topic so tu.notification_level raises; and rows with NULL notification_level make the comparison raise on NilClass. Fix: redirect to login when current_user is blank and use TopicUser.change (which creates the row if missing) instead of find_by + save!.

The unsubscribe URL is a state-mutating, token-less GET with toggle semantics (watching/tracking to regular, regular/muted to muted): corporate mail scanners and link unfurlers (Mimecast/Proofpoint-style) prefetch the URL and each fetch flips the level, so a scanner pass can downgrade watching to regular and a second fetch (or scanner plus user click) fully mutes the topic with zero user action; re-clicking an old link after re-watching downgrades again, and concurrent GETs race so one toggle is lost. Needs a confirmation step, POST, or per-user token.

The end state contradicts what the email and confirmation page promise: the email footer says 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' and the page unconditionally renders 'You will stop receiving notifications for <title>', but for watching/tracking users (the majority of recipients) the code sets regular, which still sends notifications for replies, mentions and quotes; only users already at regular/muted end up muted. Should either go straight to muted or render the message from the actual resulting level.

The unsubscribe_link locale now hard-requires %{unsubscribe_url} for every opting-in mailer: Email::MessageBuilder#html_part renders I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) for any email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true, and I18n raises MissingInterpolationArgument when the key is absent, so any other caller (e.g. digest mailer or plugins) that doesn't supply unsubscribe_url now fails to build/send the email. All add_unsubscribe_link callers need auditing.

tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so no MessageBus notification_level_change message is published to /topic/<id>: every other path that changes notification_level publishes it, meaning a tab that already has the topic open keeps showing the stale watching/tracking state (button and reason text) until a manual refresh, and the codebase now has two divergent write paths for the same state. Using TopicUser.change fixes this and the missing-row case together.

Unguarded nil dereference in `unsubscribe` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-107): the `TopicUser.find_by` result is immediately dereferenced via `tu.notification_level` with no nil check, and `current_user` itself may be nil depending on the login filter — causing a hard 500 on a URL embedded in every notification email whenever the requesting user has no `topic_users` row for the topic, with the crash occurring after the full `TopicView` materialization so every failing request pays full topic-page DB cost before erroring

`unsubscribe_link` locale (config/locales/server.en.yml:1852-1855) now contains a `%{unsubscribe_url}` placeholder, so any mailer that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without passing `unsubscribe_url` (e.g., the digest mailer) will crash at email-build time with I18n `MissingInterpolationArgument` — only `send_notification_email` was updated to pass the new arg

Topic view is materialized twice per unsubscribe click: the GET pays full show-page cost (`TopicView.new`, `MultiJson.dump` into `store_preloaded`, and `render :show`) but the Ember `topicUnsubscribe` route loads its own copy via `PostStream.loadTopicView`, so the rendered show page is never displayed, the large preloaded JSON blob is serialized and embedded but never read, and the topic may be materialized a second time server-side

State-changing GET on an email-embedded URL: `notification_level` is mutated on a plain GET (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98-115) with no confirmation step or CSRF token, making it CSRF-able against logged-in users via `` to silently mute topics, and exposing it to email scanner/prefetcher probe traffic on the site's highest-volume mail class

The new unsubscribe route (topics#unsubscribe) permanently mutates TopicUser.notification_level via a plain GET request authenticated only by the session cookie — no per-user token, no confirmation step, exempt from Rails CSRF protection, and with check_xhr explicitly skipped — so any external site can embed and silently change the notification level of every logged-in visitor
Email link scanners and AV gateways that prefetch GET URLs will trigger the unsubscribe mutation for users who merely opened the email without clicking the link

The unsubscribe action is a toggle rather than an idempotent unsubscribe: a page refresh or second fetch escalates regular → muted, so the user's final state depends on how many times the link was fetched

TopicUser.find_by result is dereferenced without a nil check (tu.notification_level immediately after find_by), raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 when the logged-in user has no TopicUser row (e.g., forwarded email, shared browser, different account) — the controller also bypasses TopicUser.change, which is the method that creates the row if missing and publishes the notification_level_change MessageBus event that open tabs rely on

The shared unsubscribe_link locale key / Email::MessageBuilder contract was changed to interpolate %{unsubscribe_url}, but template_args only contains unsubscribe_url if the caller passes it — any mail built with add_unsubscribe_link: true + html_override without the new opt now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at build time and fails to send entirely; the PR updates only one caller with no guard or fallback for other core/plugin mailers using this public builder option

Footer content drift: even when unsubscribe_url is supplied, every mail built with the add_unsubscribe_link flag now gets a topic-specific sentence appended, changing footer content for any non-topic mail that shares the flag
Logged-out users clicking the email unsubscribe link get a raw JSON 403 error body (ensure_logged_in renders JSON regardless of request format) instead of a login page redirect with a return path

The unsubscribe copy overpromises: the action only drops watching/tracking users to regular, a level that still notifies and emails the user on replies and mentions, so users who click 'stop receiving notifications' keep receiving notifications for that topic — only a second fetch reaches muted

Unchecked `TopicUser.find_by` in the unsubscribe action returns nil when the logged-in user has no TopicUser row for the topic (e.g., email link opened in a browser session logged in as a different account), causing `tu.notification_level` to raise NoMethodError and return a 500 instead of a graceful page
Direct `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, so there is no upsert and no `notification_level_change` MessageBus publish, leaving other open tabs of the topic out of sync

The `before_filter` configuration for `:unsubscribe` needs verification: if it is in an `except:` list rather than `ensure_logged_in ... only:`, `current_user` is nil for anonymous clicks and every logged-out click 500s at `current_user.id`

The unsubscribe email link is a state-changing GET with no token or confirmation that permanently mutates notification_level; mail-gateway link scanners/prefetchers and cross-site embedding (e.g., `` with no SameSite cookies) can silently mute a user's topic, and revisiting the URL keeps stepping the level down (watching → regular → muted)

The `unsubscribe_link` locale now hard-requires `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation; `I18n.t` raises MissingInterpolationArgument at email-build time inside the mailer job for any unfixed caller with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` (e.g., the digest mailer), silently failing those email sends — all callers must be audited before merging

The unsubscribe step-down logic maps watching/tracking to `regular`, which still emails the user when replied to/mentioned/quoted in that topic, contradicting the email and landing page text claiming they will stop receiving notifications; watching users must click twice to actually stop notifications

The client route `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` shows unconditional success text ('You will stop receiving notifications for title') even though no server mutation occurs when the URL is reached via client-side navigation; the success text should be conditioned on the actual `details.notification_level`
The `PostStream.loadTopicView` promise in the topic-unsubscribe route has no rejection handling for 403/404 errors (e.g., deleted or private topics)

No tests exist at all for TopicsController#unsubscribe (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98-115), the endpoint that implements the feature — nothing pins the 301 canonical-slug redirect, the notification-level transitions, the tu.save! persistence, or that the HTML response renders the topic page with the preloaded JSON the new Ember route depends on.

The per-topic unsubscribe link interpolated into emails is site-relative: Topic#url returns a relative path and nothing absolutizes the new unsubscribe_url key (unlike user_preferences_url, which MessageBuilder absolutizes), so the mailer likely interpolates '/t/slug/99/unsubscribe' into the email CTA — an anchor that cannot resolve in a mail client, leaving the feature's primary CTA dead.

No integration test renders a real send_notification_email and no unit test asserts Topic#unsubscribe_url's format, so the relative-URL problem ships green — the only spec change in the PR feeds a synthetic relative path.

spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb was patched to accommodate the new behavior rather than verify it: the only change adds unsubscribe_url to the fixture to keep old assertions passing, with no assertion that %{unsubscribe_link} is actually substituted with a cooked link containing the topic URL, and the List-Unsubscribe check is only be_present rather than verifying its value.

Making unsubscribe_url a required interpolation key is an untested breaking change to MessageBuilder's contract: any other caller or plugin using add_unsubscribe_link: true without supplying unsubscribe_url now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument.

Unhandled nil crash path: the TopicUser.find_by result is dereferenced without a nil check (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-107), so a logged-in user with no TopicUser row for the topic (e.g., a forwarded notification email) hits tu.notification_level on nil, raising NoMethodError and a 500.

No spec pins logged-out behavior for the unsubscribe action — it relies on having been appended to the ensure_logged_in only: list, and a test should assert logged-out clicks are bounced cleanly rather than 500.

The unsubscribe behavior contradicts the email/page copy: watching/tracking users are only stepped down to regular, which still sends notifications on replies/mentions, despite the copy saying 'You will stop receiving notifications' — and no test encodes the intended level-transition matrix that would have forced a decision on intended behavior.
The unsubscribe GET endpoint is non-idempotent: each repeat GET of the same URL mutates state again, stepping watching → regular → muted across refreshes or repeat clicks.

Zero frontend tests exist for the new unsubscribe route/controller/template — no QUnit unit or acceptance tests verify that the route loads the topic and renders the unsubscribe text with the fancy title, that afterModel hides the notification-reason text, or that /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe is actually recognized as the new route rather than colliding with the existing topic.fromParamsNear (/t/:slug/:id/:nearPost) pattern.

The dropdown-button conditional-title change (title now optional, empty <h4> suppressed) has no corresponding test, even though the unsubscribe page depends on the no-title path via topic-notifications-button — a regression reintroducing the unconditional <h4> would only surface visually.

New route `topicUnsubscribe` is declared after the `topic` resource whose child `fromParamsNear` (`/t/:slug/:id/:nearPost`) already matches `/t/slug/123/unsubscribe`; Ember's router recognizes in declaration order, so the unsubscribe route never activates and the new route, controller, view, template, and SCSS are unreachable dead code, while email click-throughs trigger a bogus post-stream refresh with a non-numeric nearPost

Unguarded `TopicUser.find_by` in topics_controller.rb (~line 104-106) is immediately followed by `tu.notification_level` with no nil check, causing a NoMethodError/500 for any logged-in user without an existing TopicUser row (e.g., forwarded email link, direct URL entry); a NULL notification_level would also crash the `>` comparison

The unsubscribe action hand-rolls mutation (find_by + attribute assignment + save!) instead of using the canonical `TopicUser.change` API, duplicating logic, skipping the MessageBus publish so other open tabs never learn the level changed, embedding toggle business logic in the controller, and converting validation failures into 500s

Unsubscribe is wired as a state-mutating GET with `check_xhr` explicitly skipped, so any third-party page can flip a logged-in user's notification level via `` (no CSRF protection on GET); the non-idempotent toggle is also vulnerable to prefetchers/scanners silently changing levels

Locale change to `unsubscribe_link` interpolating `%{unsubscribe_url}` creates an undocumented required mailer argument; MessageBuilder neither defaults nor validates the key, so any caller setting `add_unsubscribe_link` without `unsubscribe_url` raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at email-build time, with the API contract living implicitly in a locale file far from the code

Misspelled property name `stopNotificiationsText` ("Notificiations") in controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6, mirrored by the identical typo in templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs; works only because both sides share the typo, and grepping for "Notifications" won't find it

Route's `afterModel` mutates model state (`topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null)`) purely to suppress the `topic-notifications-button` component's reason text, coupling the route to the component's internal reading of a serialized model field; a component option/param would keep the layers decoupled

Duplicated slug-canonicalization redirect (`slugs_do_not_match || (!request_format.json? && params[:slug].blank?)`) copy-pasted from the `show` action into `unsubscribe`; two copies of URL canonicalization in the same controller will drift when one changes

Drive-by reformatting churn mixed into the feature (topic_user.rb, message_builder.rb, topic-from-params.js.es6 var→const and line shuffling, notification.html.erb re-indentation, moderator-liked/summary line reordering in routes.rb) is unrelated to per-topic unsubscribe, inflating the diff and polluting blame/bisect

No test coverage for the new mutating `unsubscribe` endpoint; the only spec touched is message_builder_spec.rb, leaving edge paths (missing TopicUser row, toggle semantics, slug redirects, anonymous handling) unexercised

The unsubscribe URL is a state-mutating, token-less GET with toggle semantics (watching/tracking to regular, regular/muted to muted): corporate mail scanners and link unfurlers (Mimecast/Proofpoint-style) prefetch the URL and each fetch flips the level, so a scanner pass can downgrade watching to regular and a second fetch (or scanner plus user click) fully mutes the topic with zero user action; re-clicking an old link after re-watching downgrades again, and concurrent GETs race so one toggle is lost. adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` (config/routes.rb) mapping to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which **mutates** `TopicUser.notification_level` and has **toggle** behavior (`> regular` -> `regular`, else -> `muted`) and `save!` (topics_controller.rb). The unsubscribe link is injected into emails via `%{unsubscribe_url}` with `post.topic.unsubscribe_url` (user_notifications.rb, topic.rb, server.en.yml) and there is no per-user token/confirmation/POST. This is a real correctness/security issue: state-changing action on GET is CSRF-able and the toggle semantics make repeated/automated GETs potentially flip/downgrade state unintentionally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The end state contradicts what the email and confirmation page promise: the email footer says 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here' and the page unconditionally renders 'You will stop receiving notifications for <title>', but for watching/tracking users (the majority of recipients) the code sets regular, which still sends notifications for replies, mentions and quotes; only users already at regular/muted end up muted. adjudication.rationale: The UI copy added in `client.en.yml` and used in `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` unconditionally promises: `You will stop receiving notifications for <title>`, and the email footer (`server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link`) says it will "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic". However, `TopicsController#unsubscribe` does not always mute the topic: it sets `tu.notification_level` to `:regular` when the current level is above regular (`if tu.notification_level > ...[:regular]`), meaning users who were watching/tracking will end up at regular, not muted. This contradicts the promised end state (full stop of topic notifications) for a common case.

All add_unsubscribe_link callers need auditing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `unsubscribe_link` (server.en.yml) to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}` in addition to `%{user_preferences_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, but `template_args` only includes `site_name`, `base_url`, `user_preferences_url` plus whatever the caller passes; there is no default for `unsubscribe_url`. That means any email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but without `unsubscribe_url` will now raise an interpolation error at render time. The PR updates one caller (`UserNotifications#send_notification_email`) and the spec, but the underlying API break is real and unguarded in the builder/locale.

Using TopicUser.change fixes this and the missing-row case together.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the diff changes `TopicUser` state via `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` followed by direct mutation and `tu.save!`. This bypasses the existing write path `TopicUser.change(...)` shown elsewhere in the diff, which publishes `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)` when `notification_level` changes. So any clients relying on that bus message won’t be notified from this code path. Additionally, `find_by` can return `nil` (no TopicUser row), and the diff does not guard against that before calling `tu.notification_level`, which would raise. Using `TopicUser.change` would also handle the missing-row case (it rescues uniqueness and creates rows).

This PR updates `send_notification_email` (and the spec) to pass `unsubscribe_url`, but the diff does not show whether *all* other callers that set `add_unsubscribe_link: true` were updated, so there’s a concrete risk of breaking email rendering unless the rest of the codebase is audited/updated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a server-side `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that builds `@topic_view = TopicView.new(...)` and then calls `perform_show_response`, which in `format.html` does `store_preloaded("topic_#{@topic_view.topic.id}", MultiJson.dump(topic_view_serializer))` and `render :show`. Separately, the new Ember route `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` defines `model(params)` that calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` to fetch and hydrate a topic client-side. adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a state-changing unsubscribe action reachable via GET. Routes add `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`, and `TopicsController#unsubscribe` mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and `save!`. The email template now includes `%{unsubscribe_url}` (set to `post.topic.unsubscribe_url`) in the unsubscribe text, so opening an email exposes a GET URL that can be auto-fetched by link scanners/prefetchers, unintentionally changing the user’s notification state without an explicit click/POST.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The unsubscribe action is a toggle rather than an idempotent unsubscribe: a page refresh or second fetch escalates regular → muted, so the user's final state depends on how many times the link was fetched

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the new action changes `TopicUser.notification_level` based on current state:
```rb
if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
  tu.notification_level = ...[:regular]
else
  tu.notification_level = ...[:muted]
end
```
This is not idempotent: a first GET can set a user from `watching/tracking` -> `regular`, and a subsequent refresh/second fetch then sets `regular` -> `muted`, so the final state depends on how many times the URL is requested. The route is wired as `get ... => topics#unsubscribe`, so refreshes/automatic prefetches can trigger the extra transition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicUser.find_by result is dereferenced without a nil check (tu.notification_level immediately after find_by), raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 when the logged-in user has no TopicUser row (e.g., forwarded email, shared browser, different account) — the controller also bypasses TopicUser.change, which is the method that creates the row if missing and publishes the notification_level_change MessageBus event that open tabs rely on

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code assigns `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and immediately dereferences it via `tu.notification_level` and later `tu.save!` with no nil guard. If no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic, this will raise `NoMethodError` and 500. The action also updates the row directly instead of using `TopicUser.change(...)`, which in this codebase is the method that handles publishing the `MessageBus` `notification_level_change` event and deals with row creation/race conditions.

Therefore, any email that uses `add_unsubscribe_link` will now get that extra topic-specific footer sentence, even if it’s not a topic notification (unless callers avoid the flag). The diff does not show other callers, so impact beyond topic notifications isn’t directly verifiable here, but the coupling is real in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Logged-out users clicking the email unsubscribe link get a raw JSON 403 error body (ensure_logged_in renders JSON regardless of request format) instead of a login page redirect with a return path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new TopicsController#unsubscribe action, routes, and email template args/links, but it does not show any authentication filter behavior (e.g., an ensure_logged_in before_filter) nor how unauthenticated requests are rendered. The claim that logged-out users receive a raw JSON 403 specifically because ensure_logged_in renders JSON regardless of request format is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The unsubscribe copy overpromises: the action only drops watching/tracking users to regular, a level that still notifies and emails the user on replies and mentions, so users who click 'stop receiving notifications' keep receiving notifications for that topic — only a second fetch reaches muted

adjudication.rationale: The new client copy says “You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}.” (config/locales/client.en.yml + topic/unsubscribe.hbs), but the server action `TopicsController#unsubscribe` only drops users with `notification_level > regular` down to `regular` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb). That does not fully align with “stop receiving notifications”, since the user is not muted on the first click if they were watching/tracking. The finding’s “second fetch” wording is imprecise (it’s a second toggle/click, not a fetch), but the core mismatch between copy and implemented state change is verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unchecked `TopicUser.find_by` in the unsubscribe action returns nil when the logged-in user has no TopicUser row for the topic (e.g., email link opened in a browser session logged in as a different account), causing `tu.notification_level` to raise NoMethodError and return a 500 instead of a graceful page
Direct `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, so there is no upsert and no `notification_level_change` MessageBus publish, leaving other open tabs of the topic out of sync

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code fetches a `TopicUser` row via `TopicUser.find_by(...)`, mutates `tu.notification_level`, and calls `tu.save!` directly. The diff shows `TopicUser.change` is the method that publishes `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)` when `notification_level` changes. By bypassing `TopicUser.change`, this new unsubscribe path will not emit the `notification_level_change` event, so other open clients/tabs subscribed to that topic channel won’t be notified of the change (and there’s also no upsert behavior here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `before_filter` configuration for `:unsubscribe` needs verification: if it is in an `except:` list rather than `ensure_logged_in ... only:`, `current_user` is nil for anonymous clicks and every logged-out click 500s at `current_user.id`

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController`, `:unsubscribe` is added to `requires_login except: [...]`, meaning the `unsubscribe` action can be hit by anonymous/logged-out users. But `def unsubscribe` immediately uses `current_user` (`TopicView.new(..., current_user)` and `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)`), which will raise when `current_user` is nil (e.g., logged-out email link click), causing a 500. The diff shows no guard or alternative authentication/token flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The unsubscribe email link is a state-changing GET with no token or confirmation that permanently mutates notification_level; mail-gateway link scanners/prefetchers and cross-site embedding (e.g., `` with no SameSite cookies) can silently mute a user's topic, and revisiting the URL keeps stepping the level down (watching → regular → muted)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a state-changing GET endpoint `GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` routed to `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (config/routes.rb), and the mailer now injects an `unsubscribe_url` into emails (user_notifications.rb + server.en.yml). `TopicsController#unsubscribe` mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and persists via `tu.save!` on a GET with no token/confirmation shown in the diff, so email link prefetchers/scanners could trigger it. The logic also makes repeated visits change state again (`> regular` -> `regular`, else -> `muted`), so revisiting can step from `regular` to `muted`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `unsubscribe_link` locale now hard-requires `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation; `I18n.t` raises MissingInterpolationArgument at email-build time inside the mailer job for any unfixed caller with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` (e.g., the digest mailer), silently failing those email sends — all callers must be audited before merging

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `unsubscribe_link` (config/locales/server.en.yml) to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part`, when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true it calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` without providing a default for `unsubscribe_url` (lib/email/message_builder.rb). This means any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but does not pass `unsubscribe_url` in opts will raise `MissingInterpolationArgument`. The diff updates one caller (`UserNotifications#send_notification_email`) and the spec to pass `unsubscribe_url`, but the diff does not show an audit of other callers, so it’s a real merge risk but not fully verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The unsubscribe step-down logic maps watching/tracking to `regular`, which still emails the user when replied to/mentioned/quoted in that topic, contradicting the email and landing page text claiming they will stop receiving notifications; watching users must click twice to actually stop notifications

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the notification level is toggled so that any level above `:regular` (e.g., tracking/watching) is only stepped down to `:regular` (not `:muted`): `if tu.notification_level > ...[:regular] ... = ...[:regular] else ... = ...[:muted]` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb). However, the new client/server copy says the user will “stop receiving notifications” for the topic (client.en.yml `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`, server.en.yml `To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic`). The diff-grounded behavior means watching/tracking users won’t be fully stopped/muted on first click and would need a second click to reach `muted`, contradicting the text.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The client route `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` shows unconditional success text ('You will stop receiving notifications for title') even though no server mutation occurs when the URL is reached via client-side navigation; the success text should be conditioned on the actual `details.notification_level`

adjudication.rationale: In the new Ember route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, the `model(params)` hook only calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` and updates a client-side `topic` record; it does not hit the new Rails mutation endpoint `TopicsController#unsubscribe`. Meanwhile the template `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` renders `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` unconditionally, and the controller computed property always returns the success text based only on `model.fancyTitle`. Therefore, if the `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` route is reached via an Ember transition (client-side navigation) rather than an initial full-page load that runs `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the UI will claim notifications were stopped even though no server-side notification_level change occurred.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `PostStream.loadTopicView` promise in the topic-unsubscribe route has no rejection handling for 403/404 errors (e.g., deleted or private topics)

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` route, the `model(params)` hook returns `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...)` with no `.catch(...)` / `error` action handling shown in this diff. So it’s accurate that 403/404 rejections (e.g., private/deleted topic) are not explicitly handled in this route and would fall back to whatever global/parent route error handling exists (not shown here). That’s a concrete edge-case/UX robustness issue, but the diff alone doesn’t prove broken behavior since Ember can handle rejected model promises via default error substates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests exist at all for TopicsController#unsubscribe (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98-115), the endpoint that implements the feature — nothing pins the 301 canonical-slug redirect, the notification-level transitions, the tu.save! persistence, or that the HTML response renders the topic page with the preloaded JSON the new Ember route depends on.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (and routes) with nontrivial behavior: canonical redirect (`redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301`), toggling `TopicUser#notification_level` and persisting via `tu.save!`, and then returning the normal topic view via `perform_show_response` (which was also changed to `render :show` for HTML). In the diff, no specs are added/updated to exercise this new controller endpoint; the only test change is in `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` for `unsubscribe_url`. So there’s nothing in this PR diff that pins the unsubscribe controller behavior the finding lists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The per-topic unsubscribe link interpolated into emails is site-relative: Topic#url returns a relative path and nothing absolutizes the new unsubscribe_url key (unlike user_preferences_url, which MessageBuilder absolutizes), so the mailer likely interpolates '/t/slug/99/unsubscribe' into the email CTA — an anchor that cannot resolve in a mail client, leaving the feature's primary CTA dead.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Topic#unsubscribe_url` as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` (app/models/topic.rb). Within this codebase, `url` appears to be a path, not an absolute URL: `relative_url` is defined to just return `url`, and email templates elsewhere explicitly prefix paths with `Discourse.base_url` (e.g. `href="<%= Discourse.base_url %><%= post.url %>"` in app/views/email/notification.html.erb). The new email i18n `unsubscribe_link` interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` directly (config/locales/server.en.yml), and the mailer passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb) without any absolutization in `Email::MessageBuilder` (lib/email/message_builder.rb). This makes it very likely the email contains a site-relative link like `/t/.../unsubscribe`, which many mail clients won’t resolve correctly, breaking the CTA.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No integration test renders a real send_notification_email and no unit test asserts Topic#unsubscribe_url's format, so the relative-URL problem ships green — the only spec change in the PR feeds a synthetic relative path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new URL plumbing for topic-specific unsubscribe: `Topic#unsubscribe_url` (app/models/topic.rb) is newly added and then passed into `send_notification_email` (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb) as `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, and the server locale now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` into the email body (config/locales/server.en.yml). However, the only spec change shown is in `message_builder_spec.rb`, which supplies a hard-coded relative path (`"/t/1234/unsubscribe"`) rather than asserting what `Topic#unsubscribe_url` actually returns, and there is no test in this diff that exercises `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` end-to-end. That’s a concrete coverage gap for the newly added behavior, even if the claimed “relative-URL problem” itself isn’t provable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb was patched to accommodate the new behavior rather than verify it: the only change adds unsubscribe_url to the fixture to keep old assertions passing, with no assertion that %{unsubscribe_link} is actually substituted with a cooked link containing the topic URL, and the List-Unsubscribe check is only be_present rather than verifying its value.

The note about `List-Unsubscribe` being only `be_present` is true but that assertion wasn’t changed by this diff, so it’s not newly introduced; still, the missing verification of the new unsubscribe URL behavior is a concrete, diff-grounded test-gap concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Making unsubscribe_url a required interpolation key is an untested breaking change to MessageBuilder's contract: any other caller or plugin using add_unsubscribe_link: true without supplying unsubscribe_url now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. adjudication_records.issue_text: The unsubscribe behavior contradicts the email/page copy: watching/tracking users are only stepped down to regular, which still sends notifications on replies/mentions, despite the copy saying 'You will stop receiving notifications' — and no test encodes the intended level-transition matrix that would have forced a decision on intended behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, the code only demotes users with notification_level > :regular (e.g., tracking/watching) down to :regular, not to :muted (it only sets :muted when current level is <= :regular). Yet the new UI/email copy explicitly says “stop receiving notifications” for the topic (client.en.yml topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications; server.en.yml unsubscribe_link). If :regular still permits topic-related notifications (e.g., replies/mentions), then the implemented transition contradicts the promised behavior. adjudication_records.issue_text: The unsubscribe GET endpoint is non-idempotent: each repeat GET of the same URL mutates state again, stepping watching → regular → muted across refreshes or repeat clicks.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) that hit `TopicsController#unsubscribe`. That action mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and saves (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`). The mutation logic is not idempotent for many starting states: e.g., if level is `> :regular` it becomes `:regular` on first GET, and a repeat GET then hits the `else` branch and sets it to `:muted` (regular -> muted). So repeated GETs can change state again, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New route `topicUnsubscribe` is declared after the `topic` resource whose child `fromParamsNear` (`/t/:slug/:id/:nearPost`) already matches `/t/slug/123/unsubscribe`; Ember's router recognizes in declaration order, so the unsubscribe route never activates and the new route, controller, view, template, and SCSS are unreachable dead code, while email click-throughs trigger a bogus post-stream refresh with a non-numeric nearPost

adjudication.rationale: In `app-route-map.js.es6`, the existing `topic` resource defines `fromParamsNear` at `/t/:slug/:id/:nearPost`. The new `topicUnsubscribe` route is added later with `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, which is also matched by the earlier dynamic `:nearPost` segment (with `nearPost = "unsubscribe"`). Given Ember route matching is sensitive to declaration order for overlapping patterns, this makes it very likely the unsubscribe URL will resolve to `topic.fromParamsNear` instead of `topicUnsubscribe`, rendering the newly added unsubscribe route/controller/view/template/SCSS effectively unreachable and potentially triggering `postStream.refresh` with a non-numeric `nearPost` (e.g. "unsubscribe").

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unguarded `TopicUser.find_by` in topics_controller.rb (~line 104-106) is immediately followed by `tu.notification_level` with no nil check, causing a NoMethodError/500 for any logged-in user without an existing TopicUser row (e.g., forwarded email link, direct URL entry); a NULL notification_level would also crash the `>` comparison

adjudication_records.issue_text: The unsubscribe action hand-rolls mutation (find_by + attribute assignment + save!) instead of using the canonical `TopicUser.change` API, duplicating logic, skipping the MessageBus publish so other open tabs never learn the level changed, embedding toggle business logic in the controller, and converting validation failures into 500s

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff shows a hand-rolled update: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)`, then `tu.notification_level = ...` and `tu.save!` (no nil-check). If no `TopicUser` row exists, `tu` will be `nil` and `tu.notification_level` will raise (500). Even when it exists, this bypasses the canonical `TopicUser.change(...)` method shown elsewhere in the diff, which publishes `MessageBus` `notification_level_change` events; skipping it can leave other open clients/tabs unaware of the change. Using `save!` also turns validation failures into 500s rather than handling them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe is wired as a state-mutating GET with `check_xhr` explicitly skipped, so any third-party page can flip a logged-in user's notification level via `` (no CSRF protection on GET); the non-idempotent toggle is also vulnerable to prefetchers/scanners silently changing levels

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that **mutates** `TopicUser.notification_level` (toggles between `:regular` and `:muted`) and persists it via `tu.save!`, but it is routed as a **GET** (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" ...`). The controller also explicitly skips `:check_xhr` for `:unsubscribe` (`skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`). Since GET requests generally bypass Rails CSRF protections and can be triggered cross-site (e.g., an ``), this makes the new endpoint CSRF-able and also susceptible to unintended toggles by prefetchers/scanners.
